messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] DEDICATED_POOL_CAPACITY CRITICAL - pool=pool-stellara-dedicated-1 tenant=Stellara region=eu-west-2 metric=gpu_utilization value=98.7% duration=3m. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/dedicated_capacity
account-rep-lena: Stellara just called support — prod requests are seeing 500s and timeouts. They say it started ~5m ago.
sre-erin: I'm on pager. Looking at cluster -- I see steady queue growth and kernel backlog. No autoscale event triggered yet. Pulling scaling policy.
eng-runtime-jay: Policy shows max_burst_gpus=4, min_reserved=12, current_active=12, queued_requests=340. They hit a sudden batch spike from internal batch job.
oncall-ml: Taking this. Any chance we can shift batch off prod?
account-rep-lena: Customer insists we don't evict anything — this is single-tenant dedicated pool, they want us to avoid impact to data residency.
ops-lead-ravi: Good — single-tenant means eviction is N/A. Options: 1) Approve emergency burst (ephemeral GPUs) 2) Trigger fast autoscale (needs infra approval) 3) Throttle non-prod jobs inside tenant. Cost & billing implications noted.
eng-runtime-jay: We can provision up to 24 ephemeral gpus in this AZ with manual override. Automated burst cap is 4 so it won't do this by itself. Need explicit approval from SRE lead or Ops.
sre-erin: I recommend emergency burst of +12 GPUs for 30m while we investigate. That should bring queue down and p99 under 1.2s. @account-rep-lena do we have verbal okay from Stellara?
account-rep-lena: On call with their infra lead — she says: "Approve any short burst that avoids errors, we'll reconcile billing." She gave verbal OK.
oncall-ml: I'll run the burst command now and monitor. Command: ```redwoodctl pools burst --pool-id pool-stellara-dedicated-1 --gpus 12 --duration 00:30 --reason "prod latency emergency" --approve````
eng-runtime-jay: Also preemptively enable lightweight model-fallback for background tasks: `deployment set --id stellara-gen --q-mode quant50 --traffic 10%` — reduces token cost for non-critical requests.
sre-erin: Executing burst (sudo) now. 
incident-bot: ACTION: burst requested by sre-erin. job_id=burst-9412345678-1. Provisioning nodes (expected ready ~90s).
sre-erin: CLI output: `OK: burst queued job_id=burst-9412345678-1 state=provisioning`
incident-bot: PROVISIONING_UPDATE job_id=burst-9412345678-1 state=ready nodes_added=12
account-rep-lena: Customer reports error rate dropping on their call. They see tail latency improving.
sre-erin: Monitoring: queue length 340 -> 42 in 2m, p50 120ms -> 85ms, p99 3.4s -> 1.05s. No other tenants affected.
ops-lead-ravi: Good outcome. Tactical notes: keep burst for 30m, then evaluate whether to extend or let autoscale handle. Post-incident: we should consider raising auto-burst cap for this customer or adding gradated thresholds. @eng-runtime-jay please estimate cost for +12gpus x30m.
eng-runtime-jay: Quick calc: 12 gpus * 0.5h * $2.40/hr ~= $14.4 (ballpark). Will run detailed invoice mapping.
oncall-ml: Leaving handoff to night oncall @sre-mike at 23:15 UTC — I'll document current state and watch for any re-queue spikes.
sre-mike: Ack taking over. Will check back in 15m.
account-rep-lena: Customer requests formal RCA and a breakdown of burst cost. Logged.
ops-lead-ravi: Postmortem items: (1) review autoscale thresholds for heavy batch spikes, (2) allow opt-in higher burst cap for enterprise contracts, (3) add quick CLI guardrails to auto-approve short bursts when customer consent present.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: pool-stellara-dedicated-1 capacity stable, burst ended as scheduled. Closing thread.
